title: C482/1210/2023 of JAMAN RAM ARYA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
C482 Application Nos.1210 of 2023,
1213 of 2023, 1216 of 2023, 1217 of
2023, 1218 of 2023, 1220 of 2023, 1222
of 2023, 1224 of 2023 and 1225 of 2023
Jaman Ram Arya ... Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Another ... Respondents
Advocate: Mr. Harshit Sanwal and Mr. Pankaj Kapil, learned counsel
for the applicant.
Mr. A.K. Sah, learned Deputy Advocate General for the
State.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
These are nine C482 Applications
preferred by the applicant-Jaman Ram Arya, who is
said to be involved in commission of offences, as it
has been provided under the Forest Conservation
Act, 1980 as well as, under the Uttar Pradesh
Forest Protection Rules and the Indian Forest Act
(Uttaranchal Amendment, 2001).

offences to be tried in Criminal Case
No.135 of 2021, "State Vs. Mohan
Chandra Joshi & Ors." under Sections 4,
10 of the Uttar Pradesh Protection of Trees
in Rural and Hill Areas Act, 1976.

4
8) In C482 No.1224 of 2023, the
applicant has been summoned in Range
Case No.05/Dwarahaat/2020-21 for the
offences to be tried in Criminal Case
No.133 of 2021, "State Vs. Mohan
Chandra Joshi & Ors." under Sections 4,
10 of the Uttar Pradesh Protection of Trees
in Rural and Hill Areas Act, 1976.
9) In C482 No.1225 of 2023, the
applicant has been summoned in Range
Case No.03/Dwarahaat/2020-21 for the
offences to be tried in Criminal Case
No.134 of 2021, "State Vs. Mohan
Chandra Joshi & Ors." under Section 26(1)
(f) of the Indian Forest Act (Uttaranchal
Amendment, 2001); under Section 2/3a of
the Forest Conservation Act, 1980; as well
as Section 26(1)(a) of the Indian Forest
Act (Uttaranchal Amendment, 2001).
2. In the attempt which has been made by
the learned counsel for the applicant to argue these
C482 Applications, few facts are not disputed, that
in relation to the project of lying down a public road
in the hills, which was to be executed by the Public
Works Department (PWD), but many trees which
were falling within the gradation line as decided by
the plan layout of PWD for the purpose of
construction of road, they would have to be

5
uprooted and that too only with the permission of
the Forest Development Corporation.
3. The present applicant has been an
employee of the Forest Development Corporation.
The allegation was that certain trees, which were
being felled in that project of lying down the road,
they were uprooted by the use of JCB and that too
without there being a requisite and proper
permission being granted and that too, the same
happened in connivance with the employees of the
Forest Development Corporation and such other
accused persons, as it has been respectively
referred to in the respective proceedings drawn,
and in the summoning order, thus, issued by the
Court of Judicial Magistrate, Dwarahaat, District
Almora.
4. There is no dispute, that prior to initiation
of the aforesaid criminal cases, an investigation was
conducted by the department itself and two reports
were submitted i.e. reports of 16.08.2020 and
22.08.2020.
5. In these reports, thus, furnished by the
concerned officers, it has been observed that the
present applicant along with the other persons, who
have also been named as co-accused persons,
have derelicted in performance of their official
duties while permitting the contractor to uproot the
trees by the use of the JCB and that too without

6
there being a valid prior permission for uprooting
the same.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has
submitted that, in case, if the reports are taken into
consideration i.e. the report of 22.08.2020 and that
of the 16.08.2020, no specific role could be said to
have been assigned to the present applicant either
to be instrumental or even having acted as a
catalyst in commission of the respective offences,
which are now the subject matter of the criminal
cases, the details of which have already been given
above.
7. He submits that all allegations of the work
which was to be performed, were to be executed by
the PWD and, it was rather the PWD which was
responsible in deployment of JCBs for the purpose
of uprooting the trees, which was otherwise
prohibited, the Forest Development Corporation or
its employees would not be held to be responsible
for the commission of offences for which the
different range cases have been registered and, on
which, the cognizance has been taken by the Court
of Judicial Magistrate, Dwarahaat, District Almora,
based on which, the C482 Applications have been
preferred.
8. In order to establish his innocence of not
being involvement in the respective commission of
offences, which are now subject matter of the

7
different criminal cases referred to above, the
learned counsel for the applicant has attempted to
draw the attention of this Court to the various
observations and the findings, which have been
recorded in the two reports to show that, in fact,
there was no direct nexus of the present applicant
in commission of offences and, hence, he cannot be
attributed to be involved, at all, in commission of
offences; but this Court is apprehensive to accept
the said argument for the reason being that, in
accordance with law, in the final report which was
submitted in relation to the respective range cases
on 12.08.2020, in its paragraph no.11, would be
relevant where, in the said reports, respective roles
have been assigned to the different accused
persons in commission of offences. Paragraph no.11
reads as under:-

9. If the said statement, recorded during the
course of submission of the final report, is taken
into consideration, i.e. the statement of the present
applicant as well as that of one Mr. Prakash Chand
Pandey, then, in fact, during the course of
investigation, the report has observed, that the

8
present applicant has admitted the fact of illegal
felling of trees by the agencies of the Public Works
Department. To what extent, in the capacity of
being an employee of the Forest Development
Corporation, the present applicant was responsible,
would be a subject matter of trial, based on
appreciating of evidence.
10. The level of connivance; the mode of
felling of trees; and the role assigned to the present
applicant; that cannot be the features, which could
be dealt with in the C482 Application, as these
aspects, which entail a consideration of evidence
and the observations made in the two reports
submitted by the officers, based on which, the
criminal proceedings have been drawn, on which
the cognizance has been taken.
11. Logically even otherwise also, this Court is
of the view that, at this stage, while exercising my
powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C., if I
venture into considering the impact of the reports,
which are the basis of the registration of the
respective range cases and the consequent criminal
cases registered against the present applicant and
also against the other co-accused persons, that will
be having a direct bearing in relation to the other
criminal cases where the other co-accused persons
have been shown to be equally involved in
commission of offences, which relate to their

9
respective criminal cases, if at all, it has been
registered against them.
12. Hence, this Court is of the view that apart
from the nature of the offences for which the
summoning order has been issued, and the
respective sentences, which it carries, they being
about six months and three months respectively
with a reasonable fine, which is to be imposed.
13. Accordingly, these C482 Applications
deserve to be disposed of with liberty left open to
the applicant to resort to his remedies, as available
to him, in accordance with law, as per the
parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in
the judgment of Satender Kumar Antil Vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation, as reported in
2022 (10) SCC 51, particularly, the guidelines
framed in paragraph no.3 (e) of the said judgment
for seeking his release on bail, as all the offences
would fall to be under 'A' category of offences.
14. Since there are as many as nine cases,
which have been registered against the present
applicant and, as per the judgment of Satender
Kumar Antil (Supra), since these offences carry a
sentence of less than seven years, the applicant is
not required to be taken into custody, rather, the
bail of applicant has to be considered, as per
parameters prescribed in paragraph no.3(e) of the
aforesaid judgment.

10
15. The apprehension expressed by the
learned counsel for the applicant is that, since there
being different complaint cases, if he is directed to
be released on bail, he will be required to furnish
sureties in each respective case. It needs no
reference, that it is now a settled law, that where
an applicant is involved in a number of criminal
cases and he is granted bail in all of them, then he
is required to furnish only two sureties, in one of
the cases, which would be read and treated as to be
a surety as against all other cases, in which the bail
is granted by the trial Court.
16. The logic behind it was that, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court and even this Court too
has considered, that it is practically impossible for
an accused/applicant, thus released on bail, to
furnish two sureties in each of the respective cases,
and if that is permitted, it would be rather an act of
futility, and the applicant would not be able to avail
the benefit of the bail granted to him in the
respective criminal cases. Hence, the two sureties
upon the grant of bail to the applicant, would be
taken as to be sureties in relation to other criminal
cases too.
17. Subject to the aforesaid, the C482
Applications are dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
